To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TiAl3 interfacial phase is responsible for the low ρc value obtained after annealing the contacts at 550°C and the TiN interfacial layer is the reason for the increase of ρc above 700°C.
the TiN/AlN interfacial transition at the Ti/Al/n-GaN contact is responsible for the observed increase in contact resistance with increasing anneal temperatures above 700°C.
the specific contact resistance (rho c) decreases with increasing anneal time and temperature up to 550 degrees Celsius and then increases again.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the microstructure and electrical properties of Al/Ti/n-GaN ohmic contacts.
the development of ohmic contact technology for n-type GaN and AlN, and the understanding of the microstructure evolution with anneal temperature.
the study of microstructural evolution and its correlation with the observed electrical behavior of Al/Ti contacts to GaN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrical behavior is dominated by the presence of AlN, which acts as a barrier to current flow.
the electrical behavior of the Ti/Al ohmics is determined by the interfacial microstructure.
the Ti/Al ohmics are stable up to 550°C, but that a transition to a TiN/AlN interfacial layer occurs between 650–700°C, resulting in the formation of a high-resistive barrier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ti/Al ohmics annealed below 650°C are dominated by TiN at the interface, and above 650°C are controlled by AlN.
the Ti/Al ohmics to n-GaN have a minimum ρc after annealing at a temperature between 550°C and 650°C.
a high density of defects at the interface is responsible for the high electrical resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TiAl3 phase is the most effective in lowering the contact resistance.
a Ti-rich interfacial layer is required for the formation of an ohmic contact to GaN, but that the Ti-rich interfacially formed layer should not be too thick.
a Ti-rich interlayer at the Al/GaN interface can be used to form ohmic contacts with a low ρc, but it is not necessary to have a TiN or AlN interlayer.
